rows.job: Read a portable millisecond clock from shell hooks.
rows.contract: mc_now_ms [PY [NOPY]] sets and prints MC_NOW_MS using the ladder EPOCHREALTIME, date +%3N, perl Time::HiRes, python (unless NOPY), whole seconds.
rows.why_single: The ladder encodes macOS and bash 3.2 behaviour learned the hard way; a second clock in a hook would skip a rung and log wrong elapsed times.
rows.coverage_limit: Shell clocks only. The perl Time::HiRes invocation must stay in the owner, and the three elapsed-timing hooks must execute mc_now_ms (delegation counts only an executed call: a command word, bare or as one quoted word, also directly after `eval`; a comment, a `type` probe, a redirection target, a `case` pattern or an argument is a mention and does not count; a command word continued over a backslash-newline is seen; a call written inside `[[ ]]`, a `for ((...))` header, an extglob group or any parenthesis that is not a subshell is skipped whole and NOT seen) and build no millisecond clock of their own: EPOCHREALTIME, `date +%s%3N`, `date +%s` in arithmetic or scaled to milliseconds (inside $(( )), times 1000, or with 000 appended), Time::HiRes, `time.time() * 1000` and `time_ns(`. `date +%s%3N` is matched as a parsed command; the other patterns are matched as text, so a string that merely spells one of them is also reported. A plain whole-second `date +%s` or `time.time()` read is NOT forbidden -- the hooks use them for watchdog and timestamp purposes that are not millisecond elapsed timing -- so another clock expression (for example $SECONDS, or a whole-second read scaled in a way the patterns do not list) is not seen. Not seen: a launcher in front of the call (`xargs`, `find -exec`, `sudo`, `env`, `timeout`, `coproc`, `command -p`), a function passed to another by name, a `$(...)` nested inside `$((...))`. Clocks in other hooks or in other languages are outside this contract.
rows.evidence: The reuse inventory design: a versioned inventory with deterministic guards for recognised second implementations (owner-ratified roadmap item; this row is a design recommendation from the external design consult, not an owner ruling on this job)

rows.job: Run the plain schema lint of the store and classify its process result.
rows.contract: mc_store_lint_schema PY MEMLINT ROOT sets MC_LINT_SCHEMA (ok | fail | engine-failure), the output and the summary flag; a bare rc=1 without memlint's own summary is an engine failure, never a finding.
rows.why_single: The pre-commit and post-commit hooks must judge a record by exactly the same rules; the invocation and verdict parsing live in one place.
rows.coverage_limit: The two commit hooks must execute mc_store_lint_schema (delegation counts only an executed call: a command word, bare or as one quoted word (`mc_store_lint_schema`, `"mc_store_lint_schema"`), also directly after `eval`; a comment, a `type` probe, a redirection target, a `case` pattern, an argument or a bare import is a mention and does not count; a command word continued over a backslash-newline is seen; a call written inside `[[ ]]`, a `for ((...))` header, an extglob group or any parenthesis that is not a subshell is skipped whole and NOT seen), so an inlined lint call that keeps the probe is caught. Forbidden direct shapes, matched against each parsed command with its `VAR=value` prefixes ignored: an interpreter (`python3`, `"$PY"`, `$MC_PY`) followed by `$MEMLINT`, `$memlint` or a `memlint.py` path, and the lint executed directly (`$memlint ROOT`, `.../memlint.py ROOT`, `$MEMLINT --...`), also behind an `env` prefix (the forbid sees it; the reach check does not, so `env mc_store_lint_...` is not seen as a call). Text that only mentions the lint (an `echo`, the owner's own arguments) is not a direct call. A third hook that runs the lint another way is only caught by the name pattern. Not seen: a launcher in front of the call (`xargs`, `find -exec`, `sudo`, `env`, `timeout`, `coproc`, `command -p`), a function passed to another by name, a `$(...)` nested inside `$((...))`, and an `eval` of anything but one plain word. A lint reached through an alias variable is not seen either.
rows.evidence: The reuse inventory design: a versioned inventory with deterministic guards for recognised second implementations (owner-ratified roadmap item; this row is a design recommendation from the external design consult, not an owner ruling on this job)
